guide.summary: A base design system bridging Figma and React code.
guide.description: Simple Design System (SDS) shows how Figma variables, styles, components and Code Connect map to a React codebase. This saved snapshot includes the original tokens and component stories, with local guidance and editable token values.
guide.principles:
Use existing SDS components and their supported props. Check the source example before composing a new interface.

Use semantic SDS variables for colors, typography, spacing, radii and shadows. Propose a named token when the system is missing a value.

Use Section, Flex and Grid for layout. Compose existing primitives before adding new patterns.

Keep component behavior honest: names, variants and states should match the React source. Preview light and dark themes and test keyboard interactions.

Use ButtonDanger for destructive actions. Give icon-only actions accessible names and fields visible labels.

componentNotes.src/stories/primitives/Button.stories.ts: Use primary for the main action, neutral for secondary actions and subtle for lower emphasis. Sizes: small or medium. Use ButtonDanger for destructive actions. Children supply the label and icons. The component delegates interactions to React Aria: use onPress for button actions. Supplying href renders a link.
For destructive actions only. Choose danger-primary or danger-subtle; use small or medium sizing. Provide a clear action label.
Group related actions with align: start, end, center, justify or stack. Inspect the source story for composition.
componentNotes.src/stories/primitives/Input.stories.tsx: Use a visible label and helpful description. Explore disabled and required states in the controls. The preview is an interactive example; it does not submit data.
